commit.message:
Update the walkthrough link

Points at the re-cut video that matches the running deployment.

Re-cut the walkthrough against the enclave the site actually runs

The footage was recorded before the key moved into KMS, so the seal and the
proof page in it named an earlier boot while the site named this one. Everything
now refers to the same measured image and the same signing key, and the record
cites the two transactions the recording itself sent.

The film also gained the piece that was missing from it: where the key comes
from, why the address never changes, and why that is what lets the machine sleep
between borrowers.

Give the enclave a key that outlives it, and let it sleep

An enclave that minted a fresh key on every boot could never be trusted for
long: each restart needed another setTeeAddress, and whoever sent that
transaction became a second thing to trust. The key is now minted inside the
TEE, wrapped by Cloud KMS and stored only in wrapped form; later boots get it
back by authenticating with their own attestation through Workload Identity
Federation, whose provider only accepts tokens carrying the expected measured
image, CONFIDENTIAL_SPACE, GCP_AMD_SEV and secure boot. Run a modified image and
the measurement changes, KMS declines, and the enclave falls back to an
ephemeral key the oracle refuses — it can sign all it likes and nothing lands.

With a stable identity the machine no longer has to stay up. It exits after
twenty idle minutes, and the interface starts it again when a borrower needs a
line, saying what it is waiting for while a Confidential Space VM boots. The
credentials that do the starting carry two permissions and hold nothing the
protocol depends on.

The record now cites the run this enclave performed end to end.

Link the walkthrough, and say plainly what needs a live enclave

Two minutes of footage answers more than the README can. Alongside it, an
explicit note on what stays verifiable when no enclave is running — everything
already on-chain — and what does not: issuing a new line, because the signature
that makes one usable exists only inside the machine.

Report what the chain did, and stop asking it nine times

A reverted transaction never arrives as data: wagmi re-simulates the call to
explain the failure and throws, so the refusal came back on the error branch
while the interface fell through to its default and announced the loan as
drawn. It now reads the settlement explicitly — funded, refused, still landing,
or unreadable — and names the error the chain actually raised instead of the one
we expected. A draw is only ever called drawn when a receipt says so.

The pages were also firing a request per read, which the public endpoint
eventually answered with 429s and blank fields. Coston2 carries Multicall3 at
the canonical address; declaring it turns a page load into a single call.

The record of proceedings now cites the transactions in the walkthrough, so the
receipts on screen and the table underneath refer to the same four events.

Re-run the whole proof against a freshly attested enclave

A new Confidential Space boot on the same measured image, a new signing key bound
into its attestation, and the four steps done again end to end: the key was
registered, the enclave signed an eight-dollar line, a borrower drew against it
with no collateral, and the draw that went past it reverted.

The record now comes from one boot rather than being assembled across runs, so
the signing key on the page, the key the oracle trusts, and every receipt in the
table all refer to the same machine. The lede quotes the figures that were
actually scored.

The attestation says dbgstat: enabled and the proof page now says so too, with
the reason: this is the debug Confidential Space image, which is what makes the
boot log readable from outside.

Point the docs at the hosted demo, and give it a mark of its own

A reviewer can now start from a page that reads the live deployment instead of
from a contract address, so JUDGES.md opens there. The icon is the two motifs
the interface is built on: a redaction bar, and the ceiling it stops at.

Web: apply for a line — the enclave signs it, the borrower publishes it

Seven figures go to the enclave through a server-side route, so the page can be
served over HTTPS while the enclave is not, and the enclave carries no CORS
headers for a browser. Nothing is relayed on the borrower's behalf: what comes
back is a signature, and they submit it from their own wallet.

Before that costs gas, the page recovers the signer the same way CreditOracle
does — hash the result with the action id, the tag and the status, recover from
the EIP-191 signature — and says plainly whether the oracle will accept it.

An enclave that produced no attestation token gets a stamp that says so. A
signature alone is not a seal, and the interface does not lend it credibility
the machine has not earned.

Web: stop clipping the over-the-line label, and seal the ticket's unit strip

The zone past the ceiling is scaled, so a draw that only just exceeds the line
left a sliver too narrow to hold its own label. It now reserves enough width to
read — the distance past the ceiling was never a quantity worth measuring.

The unit strip sat centred in the ticket rather than filling it, leaving the
sheet showing through above and below it.

Web: the borrower's file, the lender's pool, and the seal behind them

Reads the live deployment on Coston2 — the attested line from CreditOracle, the
position and pool from VeilMarket, prices from the FTSO feeds the market itself
uses. A draw is measured against the ceiling before it is signed; when it goes
past, the interface says so and still offers to send it, because the refusal
belongs to the market contract.

Writes that read a price feed carry an explicit gas limit: estimation comes in
under the real cost of the FTSO read and the transaction dies after the price
comes back.

Enclave: allow the demo-borrower env override and emit a signed bundle at boot

Adds the Confidential Space launch-policy label so the launcher may inject DEMO_BORROWER, and, when it is set, scores that borrower at boot and prints the signed credit-line bundle to the serial console — so the on-chain walkthrough can be driven from attested output without opening a network path to the enclave.

Point docs at the live deployment scored by a real Confidential Space enclave

Updates the README, JUDGES walkthrough, and SDK to the current CreditOracle and VeilMarket, and to the on-chain trail where a real GCP Confidential Space (AMD SEV) enclave's attested key is set, its signed credit line is accepted, an under-collateralized FXRP loan is drawn, and an over-limit draw is refused. Drops the stand-in-signer demo script now that the real flow is on-chain.

Extract a shared core module and add the deployable enclave

The scoring, clearing, wire, and processor packages move into a standalone github.com/rayyer/veil-core module (go-ethereum only) that builds and tests without the tee-node toolchain; the extension now consumes it. The new enclave/ is the deployable Confidential Space service: it generates a signing key in the TEE, attests it via the Confidential Space launcher, and serves /score, which evaluates a borrower and signs the verdict exactly as CreditOracle verifies it. A self-check confirms the signature recovers to the enclave address over the on-chain digest.

Harden the market: lock minimum liquidity and reject stale prices

Two fixes from a self-review. deposit() locks a minimum of shares on the first deposit so an empty pool can't be seeded with a dust share and inflated by a donation to round later depositors to zero. _prices() now rejects a zero or stale FTSO reading, which would otherwise value debt at nothing and let a borrow exceed its true limit. Adds tests for both, plus a share-inflation-resistance case; the live-oracle fork test still passes.

Add JUDGES.md: a five-minute reviewer walkthrough

Guides a reviewer straight to the verified contracts, the on-chain flow (attest, borrow, refusal), the tests, and the exact files where the enclave-signs / contract-enforces trust boundary lives.

Wire confidential scoring and clearing into the Flare Compute Extension

The extension decrypts a borrower's financials inside the enclave (ECIES via the tee-node sign server), reads the authenticated borrower from the on-chain envelope, scores or clears, and returns a result the node signs. Two operations: CREDIT/SCORE and AUCTION/CLEAR. Builds against Flare's tee-node as a sibling per the Compute Extension layout; see extension/README.md.
Write the project README: problem, architecture, live deployment, proofs

Add reference integration and TypeScript SDK for the credit oracle

ReferenceLendingPool is a standalone example that lends against a borrower's attested credit line through ICreditOracle, showing the oracle is a primitive any Flare protocol can consume (5 tests). The @veil/sdk package reads the oracle and market on Coston2 and ABI-encodes a credit request into the exact layout the enclave decodes; it reads the live deployment end-to-end.

Add end-to-end demo script driving the deployed Coston2 contracts

Attests a credit line, draws FXRP under-collateralized within it, and (paired with the over-cap send in the walkthrough) shows the on-chain refusal. Uses a demo signer that CreditOracle.setTeeAddress swaps for the real enclave key once the extension is live.

Bind the credit-score request to the authenticated caller

requestCreditScore now wraps the encrypted financials with msg.sender in the on-chain envelope, so the enclave scores the caller's own address rather than a self-asserted one in the ciphertext. The financials stay encrypted; only the borrower address (already public as the tx sender) is in the clear.

Add Coston2 deploy script for the Veil core

Deploys CreditOracle and VeilMarket wired to the live FtsoV2 oracle, the real FXRP token, and the XRP/USD and FLR/USD feeds. The enclave signing address is set post-deploy via setTeeAddress, so the oracle needs no redeploy once the extension is running.

Add fork test: enforce the credit line against the live Coston2 FTSO price

Deploys VeilMarket against the real FtsoV2 on a Coston2 fork and confirms a borrow is refused once its USD value at the live XRP/USD feed exceeds the confidential credit line. Proves the oracle integration end-to-end with no mock price.

Assemble the enclave pipelines: confidential scoring and sealed-bid clearing

processor wires the deterministic engines to the on-chain wire format. ProcessCreditScore decodes a borrower's decrypted financials, scores them, and encodes a verdict bound to the caller's authenticated address (never the payload). ProcessClearing decodes sealed lender bids, clears them at a uniform price, and encodes the outcome. Both are transport-agnostic so the Flare Compute Extension glue wraps them unchanged. wire gains ABI codecs for the request and clearing shapes. 6 new tests.

Add ABI wire bridge between the enclave and the on-chain decoder

Encodes a credit verdict into exactly the bytes CreditOracle.submitCreditLine decodes (address, uint256 18-dec USD, uint8, uint64, uint64), verified byte-for-byte against a cast-generated Solidity abi.encode vector so the enclave signature covers precisely what the contract verifies. Round-trip and scaling tests included.

Add enclave core: deterministic credit scoring and sealed-bid clearing

Two pure, integer-only, fully-explainable engines that run inside the TEE. scoring turns private borrower financials into a credit line and score band from named, auditable factors (payment history, DTI, reserves, history length, defaults). clearing runs a uniform-price sealed-bid auction over lenders' encrypted rate bids, filling a target at the marginal accepted rate. Both are deterministic (integer math, stable tie-breaks) so their verdicts can be checked against a fixed answer key. 13 Go tests.

Add VeilInstructionSender: dispatch confidential-compute instructions to the TEE registry

On-chain entry point routing credit-score (CREDIT/SCORE) and sealed-bid clearing (AUCTION/CLEAR) requests through the Flare TEE extension registry, with encrypted payloads passed opaquely. Minimal registry interfaces vendored; 4 tests cover op-type dispatch, the extension-id lifecycle, and constructor guards.

Add VeilMarket: under-collateralized FXRP lending against attested credit

Two-sided market: lenders supply FXRP for shares; borrowers draw FXRP up to native-C2FLR collateral value (FTSO FLR/USD) plus their confidential credit line (CreditOracle), with debt priced by FTSO XRP/USD. Borrows beyond borrowing power revert. Index-based interest, and liquidation when a position goes underwater — including when a credit line expires. 13 tests; FtsoV2/credit/token injected via interfaces for isolated unit testing.

Bootstrap Veil: CreditOracle with TEE-attestation verification

Foundry project wired to Flare periphery (Coston2) and OpenZeppelin. CreditOracle verifies the enclave's EIP-191 signature over the Flare Compute Extension result hash and publishes per-borrower credit lines, failing closed on wrong signer, bad status, expiry, replay, or tampering. 7 passing tests cover the happy path and each rejection.
